greek: προσκαλεσάμενος δὲ Ισαακ τὸν Ιακωβ εὐλόγησεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐνετείλατο αὐτῷ λέγων Οὐ λήμψῃ γυναῖκα ἐκ τῶν θυγατέρων Χανααν·
hint: Isaac calls Jacob and blesses him and charges him: Do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan;

notes.text: The middle of προσκαλέω, *to call to oneself*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[having called to himself|having called to himself, having called to one, having called to his aid, having cited|προσκαλέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ισαακ]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[spoke well of|spoke well of, praised, honoured, blessed|εὐλογέω]] him and [[enjoined|enjoined, commanded|ἐντέλλομαι]] to him [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] not [[you will take|you will take, you will receive, you will take hold of and grasp and seize|λαμβάνω]] [[woman|woman, mistress and lady, wife and spouse, mortal woman|γυνή]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of the daughters [[name:Χανααν]];

(Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)

greek: ἀναστὰς ἀπόδραθι εἰς τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν εἰς τὸν οἶκον Βαθουηλ τοῦ πατρὸς τῆς μητρός σου καὶ λαβὲ σεαυτῷ ἐκεῖθεν γυναῖκα ἐκ τῶν θυγατέρων Λαβαν τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ τῆς μητρός σου.
hint: get up and run away to Mesopotamia, to the house of Bethuel your mother's father, and take a wife from there from the daughters of Laban your mother's brother.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *paddenâ ʾărām*, *to Paddan-aram*, as at 25:20.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds Συρίας; the Berlin papyrus, 911, does not.

reading: [[having stood up|having stood up, having risen, having risen to fight against, having risen to go and set out|ἀνίστημι]] [[run away|run away, run off, escape|ἀποδιδράσκω]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Μεσοποταμίαν]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the house|the house, the abode and dwelling, the room and chamber, the house of a god and temple, the household goods and substance, the household and family|οἶκος]] [[name:Βαθουηλ]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather|πατήρ]] [[of the mother|of the mother, of the dam, of the source|μήτηρ]] of you and [[take|take, receive, take hold of and grasp and seize|λαμβάνω]] for yourself [[from that place|from that place, thence, thereafter, next|ἐκεῖθεν]] [[woman|woman, mistress and lady, wife and spouse, mortal woman|γυνή]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of the daughters [[name:Λαβαν]] [[of the son of the same mother|of the son of the same mother, of the brother, of the near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] [[of the mother|of the mother, of the dam, of the source|μήτηρ]] of you.

names.gloss: (Μεσοποταμία, Greek, "the land between the rivers", for Hebrew Paddan-ʾĂrām)
(Βαθουηλ, from Hebrew Bĕtûʾēl, of uncertain meaning)

greek: ὁ δὲ θεός μου εὐλογήσαι σε καὶ αὐξήσαι σε καὶ πληθύναι σε, καὶ ἔσῃ εἰς συναγωγὰς ἐθνῶν·
hint: And may my God bless you and increase you and multiply you, and you will become gatherings of nations;

notes.text: Three aorist optatives, the wish, as δῴη at 27:28.
συναγωγή is first *a bringing together, uniting*.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] of me [[may he speak well of|may he speak well of, may he praise, may he honour, may he bless|εὐλογέω]] you and [[may he make large|may he make large, may he increase, may he augment, may he increase in power and strengthen and exalt and aggrandise, may he promote to honour and glorify and magnify|αὐξάνω]] you and [[may he make full|may he make full, may he increase, may he multiply|πληθύνω]] you, and you will be [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[bringings together|bringings together, unitings, places of assembly and synagogues, drawings together and contractings|συναγωγή]] [[of numbers of people accustomed to live together|of numbers of people accustomed to live together, of companies and bodies of men, of hosts, of swarms and flocks, of nations and peoples, of nations and gentiles, of special classes, of castes and tribes, of sexes|ἔθνος]];

greek: καὶ δῴη σοι τὴν εὐλογίαν Αβρααμ τοῦ πατρός μου, σοὶ καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου μετὰ σέ, κληρονομῆσαι τὴν γῆν τῆς παροικήσεώς σου, ἣν ἔδωκεν ὁ θεὸς τῷ Αβρααμ.
hint: and may he give you the blessing of Abraham my father, to you and to your offspring after you, to inherit the land of your sojourning, which God gave to Abraham.

notes.text: παροίκησις, one sense, *a neighbourhood*, of the land where one dwells beside.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads δέδωκεν, the perfect.

reading: and [[may he give|may he give, may he grant, may he provide, may he give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to you [[the good language|the good language, the fine language, the fair speech and specious talk, the eulogy and panegyric, the blessing|εὐλογία]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather|πατήρ]] of me, to you and [[to that which is sown|to that which is sown, to the seed, to the germ and origin and element, to the offspring and issue, to the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of you [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] you, [[to receive a share of an inheritance|to receive a share of an inheritance and inherit a portion, to inherit, to be an inheritor, to succeed|κληρονομέω]] [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] of the neighbourhood of you, which [[gave|gave, granted, provided, gave over and delivered up|δίδωμι]] [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] to [[name:Αβρααμ]].

names.gloss: (Αβρααμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrāhām, which the Hebrew of 17:5 hears in ʾab hămôn gôyim, "father of a multitude of nations")

greek: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν Ισαακ τὸν Ιακωβ, καὶ ἐπορεύθη εἰς τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν πρὸς Λαβαν τὸν υἱὸν Βαθουηλ τοῦ Σύρου ἀδελφὸν δὲ Ρεβεκκας τῆς μητρὸς Ιακωβ καὶ Ησαυ.
hint: Isaac sends Jacob off, and he goes to Mesopotamia, to Laban son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah the mother of Jacob and Esau.

notes.text: δέ inside the phrase, as often: *and the brother of Rebekah*.

reading: and [[sent off|sent off, sent away, banished, despatched, went away and departed|ἀποστέλλω]] [[name:Ισαακ]] [[name:Ιακωβ]], and [[was driven|was driven, was carried, went, walked, marched, went across and passed|πορεύομαι]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Μεσοποταμίαν]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Λαβαν]] the son [[name:Βαθουηλ]] [[name:Σύρου]] [[son of the same mother|a son of the same mother, a brother, a near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ρεβεκκας]] [[of the mother|of the mother, of the dam, of the source|μήτηρ]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] and [[name:Ησαυ]].

names.gloss: (Σύρος, the man of Συρία, Syria; the Hebrew has ʾărammî, the Aramean)
(Ρεβεκκα, from Hebrew Ribqâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Ησαυ, from Hebrew ʿĒśāw, usually connected with śēʿār, "hair")

greek: Εἶδεν δὲ Ησαυ ὅτι εὐλόγησεν Ισαακ τὸν Ιακωβ καὶ ἀπῴχετο εἰς τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν Συρίας λαβεῖν ἑαυτῷ ἐκεῖθεν γυναῖκα ἐν τῷ εὐλογεῖν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐνετείλατο αὐτῷ λέγων Οὐ λήμψῃ γυναῖκα ἀπὸ τῶν θυγατέρων Χανααν,
hint: Esau sees that Isaac blessed Jacob and sent him off to Mesopotamia of Syria to take a wife from there, and that in blessing him he charged him: Do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,

notes.text: ἐν with the articular infinitive, `in the speaking well of`, as at 24:52.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone leaves it out.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

names.gloss: (Συρία, the Greek name of the land; the Hebrew here is Paddan-ʾĂrām)

greek: καὶ ἤκουσεν Ιακωβ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπορεύθη εἰς τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν Συρίας,
hint: and Jacob listened to his father and mother and went to Mesopotamia of Syria,

notes.text: [[flag]] The Berlin papyrus, 911, has it; Codex Alexandrinus leaves it out.

hint: and Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were evil in the eyes of Isaac his father,

hint: and Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son, sister of Nebaioth, as a wife besides his wives.

notes.text: πρός with the dative, *beside*, of what is added.

hint: Jacob went out from the Well of the Oath and travelled to Haran.

notes.text: The place named at 26:33, Beersheba.

reading: And [[went out of|went out of, came out, went away and marched off, went forth|ἐξέρχομαι]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the well|of the well, of the tank and cistern and reservoir, of the oil jar|φρέαρ]] [[of the object by which one swears|of the object by which one swears, of the witness of an oath, of the oath|ὅρκος]] and [[was driven|was driven, was carried, went, walked, marched, went across and passed|πορεύομαι]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Χαρραν]].

greek: καὶ ἀπήντησεν τόπῳ καὶ ἐκοιμήθη ἐκεῖ· ἔδυ γὰρ ὁ ἥλιος· καὶ ἔλαβεν ἀπὸ τῶν λίθων τοῦ τόπου καὶ ἔθηκεν πρὸς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκοιμήθη ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ἐκείνῳ.
hint: He came upon a place and slept there, for the sun had set; and he took one of the stones of the place and put it at his head and slept in that place.

notes.text: ἀπαντάω with the dative, *to meet*.
δύω, whose first sense is *to strip off*; of the sun, *to sink, set*.
πρός with the genitive, *at the head*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ἐπέθηκεν.

greek: καὶ ἐνυπνιάσθη, καὶ ἰδοὺ κλίμαξ ἐστηριγμένη ἐν τῇ γῇ, ἧς ἡ κεφαλὴ ἀφικνεῖτο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι τοῦ θεοῦ ἀνέβαινον καὶ κατέβαινον ἐπʼ αὐτῆς.
hint: And he dreamed: a ladder fixed in the earth, whose top reached to heaven, and the angels of God going up and coming down on it.

notes.text: στηρίζω in the perfect passive, the standing state, as at 27:37.
No Middle Liddell entry; LSJ's ἐνυπνιάζω is *dream*, and MorphGNT files the middle.

greek: ὁ δὲ κύριος ἐπεστήρικτο ἐπʼ αὐτῆς καὶ εἶπεν Ἐγὼ κύριος ὁ θεὸς Αβρααμ τοῦ πατρός σου καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ισαακ· μὴ φοβοῦ· ἡ γῆ, ἐφʼ ἧς σὺ καθεύδεις ἐπʼ αὐτῆς, σοὶ δώσω αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου.
hint: And the Lord was leaning on it and said: I am the Lord, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac; do not be afraid; the land you are sleeping on I will give to you and to your offspring.

notes.text: ἐπιστηρίζω in the pluperfect, the standing state in the past.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus leaves out the second κύριος; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has it.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς γῆς καὶ πλατυνθήσεται ἐπὶ θάλασσαν καὶ ἐπὶ λίβα καὶ ἐπὶ βορρᾶν καὶ ἐπʼ ἀνατολάς, καὶ ἐνευλογηθήσονται ἐν σοὶ πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐν τῷ σπέρματί σου.
hint: And your offspring will be like the sand of the earth and will spread to the sea and to the south-west and to the north and to the east, and in you and in your offspring all the tribes of the earth will be blessed.

notes.text: The Hebrew is *kaʿăpar hāʾāreṣ*, *as the dust of the earth*. The Greek has ἄμμος, *sand*.
φυλή, the chain of GEN 10:18: the tribes, where 22:18 has τὰ ἔθνη.

greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ μετὰ σοῦ διαφυλάσσων σε ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ πάσῃ, οὗ ἐὰν πορευθῇς, καὶ ἀποστρέψω σε εἰς τὴν γῆν ταύτην, ὅτι οὐ μή σε ἐγκαταλίπω ἕως τοῦ ποιῆσαί με πάντα, ὅσα ἐλάλησά σοι.
hint: And here I am with you, guarding you in every way you go, and I will bring you back to this land, for I will not leave you until I have done all that I have told you.

notes.text: *Wherever you go*, ἐάν after the relative adverb.
The double negative with the aorist subjunctive, as at 24:33.

greek: καὶ ἐξηγέρθη Ιακωβ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπεν ὅτι Ἔστιν κύριος ἐν τῷ τόπῳ τούτῳ, ἐγὼ δὲ οὐκ ᾔδειν.
hint: Jacob woke from his sleep and said: The Lord is in this place, and I did not know it.

notes.text: The pluperfect of οἶδα, the chain of GEN 3:5.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ ἐφοβήθη καὶ εἶπεν Ὡς φοβερὸς ὁ τόπος οὗτος· οὐκ ἔστιν τοῦτο ἀλλʼ ἢ οἶκος θεοῦ, καὶ αὕτη ἡ πύλη τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
hint: And he was afraid and said: How fearful is this place; this is nothing but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.

notes.text: ὡς in exclamation, *how*: the adverb, not the comparative conjunction.
θεός without the article, the chain of GEN 1:2.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ ἀνέστη Ιακωβ τὸ πρωὶ καὶ ἔλαβεν τὸν λίθον, ὃν ὑπέθηκεν ἐκεῖ πρὸς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔστησεν αὐτὸν στήλην καὶ ἐπέχεεν ἔλαιον ἐπὶ τὸ ἄκρον αὐτῆς.
hint: Jacob got up in the morning and took the stone he had put at his head and set it up as a pillar and poured oil on its top.

notes.text: στήλη is first *a block of stone*, then *a monument, gravestone*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἔθηκεν; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has ὑπέθηκεν.

greek: καὶ ἐκάλεσεν Ιακωβ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου Οἶκος θεοῦ· καὶ Ουλαμλους ἦν ὄνομα τῇ πόλει τὸ πρότερον.
hint: And Jacob called the name of that place House of God; and the city's name before that was Ulamlous.

notes.text: The Greek of the Hebrew Bêt-ʾĒl, Bethel, printed as the name, with Rahlfs's capital.
[[flag]] Rahlfs prints Ουλαμλους; Codex Alexandrinus reads ουλαμμαυς.

greek: καὶ ηὔξατο Ιακωβ εὐχὴν λέγων Ἐὰν ᾖ κύριος ὁ θεὸς μετʼ ἐμοῦ καὶ διαφυλάξῃ με ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ταύτῃ, ᾗ ἐγὼ πορεύομαι, καὶ δῷ μοι ἄρτον φαγεῖν καὶ ἱμάτιον περιβαλέσθαι
hint: And Jacob vowed a vow: If the Lord God is with me and guards me on this way I am going, and gives me bread to eat and clothing to put on,
